title: Relaxation-Rectified Anti-Jaynes-Cummings Cascades for Autonomous Fock-State Stabilization
abstract: We propose an autonomous scheme for stabilizing prescribed Fock states in a Kerr cavity by rectifying anti-Jaynes--Cummings interactions with auxiliary-qubit relaxation. Full Lindblad simulations demonstrate steady states dominated by the Fock states $|1\rangle$ through $|4\rangle$, accompanied by pronounced Wigner negativity. An analytical birth--death model captures the steady-state populations and identifies the operating regime for stabilization. These results establish auxiliary-qubit relaxation as a resource for autonomous reservoir engineering and provide a route to nonclassical bosonic-state preparation in a single Kerr cavity and, through a boundary reservoir, in a Kerr-cavity chain.
summary: The authors present a method to autonomously stabilize Fock states in a Kerr cavity by coupling it to auxiliary qubits. They use qubit relaxation to rectify the anti-Jaynes-Cummings interaction, creating a directed, photon-number selective cascade. This establishes a powerful resource for reservoir engineering, enabling nonclassical bosonic state preparation.
main_problem: The paper proposes an autonomous scheme to stabilize specific Fock states within a Kerr cavity by engineering interactions with auxiliary qubits.
main_result: The combination of anti-Jaynes-Cummings interactions and qubit relaxation successfully creates a directed, photon-number selective cascade, leading to stable, nonclassical Fock state populations.
method: The dynamics are analyzed using the Lindblad master equation, supplemented by an analytical birth-death model for steady-state population tracking.
model_or_system: The system consists of a Kerr cavity mode coupled to an array of $N_q$ auxiliary qubits. The evolution is governed by a master equation incorporating Kerr nonlinearity and engineered Anti-Jaynes-Cummings (AJC) interactions.
key_observables: Steady-state Fock state populations ($P_{ss}^n$) and the presence of Wigner negativity ($N_W$).
important_parameters: Qubit relaxation rate ($\gamma$), cavity loss ($\kappa$), Kerr nonlinearity ($K$), and detuning ($\Delta_\ell$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the rectification of reversible AJC exchange via irreversible qubit relaxation, and the BD model is an approximation valid in certain regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the process flow (Fig. 1), the time evolution of Fock-state populations towards the target state (Fig. 2), the dependence of steady-state populations on various parameters (Fig. 3), and the resulting Wigner negativity (Fig. 4).
paper_structure: The paper develops the effective Hamiltonian via transformations (rotating frame, RWA), derives the dynamics using the Lindblad equation, analyzes the steady-state populations using a birth-death model, and finally investigates parameter robustness.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable mechanism for reservoir engineering in cavity QED, demonstrating how engineered dissipation can drive a system towards nonclassical quantum states like Fock states.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Dissipation-rectified Fock-state preparation. (a) A Kerr cavity mode is coupled to Nq relaxing auxiliary qubits through independently driven blue-sideband interactions. (b) For each qubit ℓ, coherent coupling followed by qubit relax- ation produces the net photon-raising transition |ℓ⟩→|ℓ+1⟩. (c) Cascading these processes pumps the cavity from |0⟩to the target state |Nq⟩, while further raising is off resonance. Blue, green, and gray arrows denote coherent blue-sideband transitions or the resulting raising processes, qubit relaxation, and off-resonant leakage, respectively.

FIG. 2. Time evolution of the cavity Fock-state populations for target states |1⟩, |2⟩, |3⟩, and |4⟩in panels (a)–(d), re- spectively. Different colors denote the populations Pn(t) of the corresponding Fock states |n⟩. Solid curves show the full numerical Lindblad dynamics, while open circles denote the corresponding analytical BD results. Insets show the Wigner functions of the stabilized cavity states, with the correspond- ing Wigner negativities NW indicated. The parameters are K/g = 100, κ/g = 0.05, and γ/g = 3.

FIG. 3. Steady-state target-state populations P ss n for |n⟩= |1⟩, |2⟩, |3⟩, and |4⟩as functions of (a) the qubit relaxation rate γ/g, (b) the cavity loss rate κ/g, (c) the Kerr nonlin- earity K/g, and (d) the common detuning δcom/g. Different colors correspond to different target Fock states. Solid curves show the full numerical Lindblad results, while open circles denote the corresponding analytical BD results. The fixed parameters are K/g = 100, κ/g = 0.05, and γ/g = 3, except for the quantity varied in each panel. In (c), the qubits are retuned according to ∆ℓ= −(2ℓ+ 1)K as K is varied; in (d), ∆ℓ= −(2ℓ+ 1)K + δcom.

FIG. 4. Steady-state Wigner negativity NW of the stabilized single-photon state over different parameter planes. (a) NW versus K/g and γ/g at κ/g = 0.05. (b) NW versus κ/g and γ/g at K/g = 100. (c) NW versus κ/g and K/g at γ/g = 3. When K is varied, the qubit is retuned according to ∆0 = −K to maintain resonance with the target |0, g0⟩↔|1, e0⟩ transition. All panels share the same color scale.

FIG. 5. Extension of autonomous Fock-state stabilization to a Kerr-cavity chain. (a) The primary mode ˆa0 ≡ˆa, directly coupled to Nq auxiliary qubits, is connected to Nc−1 identical lossy Kerr modes through nearest-neighbor beam-splitter in- teractions of strength G. (b),(c) Local steady-state Fock-state populations of the individual cavities for (Nq, Nc) = (2, 2) and (1, 3), respectively. In the indirectly coupled cavities, the population of the same target Fock state as in the primary cavity ˆa0 is dominant, demonstrating the extension of the sta- bilization along the chain. The parameters are K/g = 100, G/g = 1, γ/g = 3, κ/g = 0.01, and δcom/g = 0.
